system_description.narrative_title: Fragmentation, tech disruption and resource shocks reshaping the world order
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system driven by overlapping security conflicts, a fast-moving technology competition (especially AI and data infrastructure), and volatile economic and energy markets. Feedbacks between wars, commodity flows and domestic politics (populist leaders, polarized democracies) amplify shocks, while regulatory and institutional responses struggle to keep pace. This produces regional spillovers, market volatility and accelerating strategic competition among major powers.
system_description.scope: Interacting processes of state and alliance security (kinetic and hybrid warfare), global energy and commodity flows, international finance and capital markets, the transnational tech/AI and data-centre ecosystem, migration and humanitarian flows, transnational legal and institutional responses, and domestic political volatility that shapes foreign policy.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio‑economic‑ecological system (the global human system in which politics, economy, technology and environment interact)
adjacent_subsystems: Regional security architectures (NATO, Gulf security, Indo‑Pacific balances)
Global financial markets and sovereign/debt architecture
Global technology and data‑infrastructure ecosystem (AI hyperscalers, chip supply chains, cloud/data centres)
Energy and maritime supply chains (oil, shipping routes, chokepoints)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: A sustained high‑intensity conflict between Russia and Ukraine, marked by front‑line strikes, ceasefire diplomacy and growing NATO support that is reshaping European security calculations.

variables.name: Iran‑backed regional escalation
variables.description: Iran and its proxy networks (notably in Yemen and the Levant) are intensifying cross‑border strikes and asymmetric operations against Gulf Arab and regional targets, altering deterrence and coalition responses in the Middle East.

variables.name: Global energy supply risk
variables.description: A wave of attacks, shipping disruptions and strategic supply agreements is driving acute volatility in oil and refined‑fuel flows, forcing states and firms to reroute supplies and rethink energy security arrangements.

variables.name: AI computing and chip race
variables.description: A competition among U.S. tech giants, chipmakers and international rivals (including Chinese firms) over GPUs, custom AI silicon, investment and access to compute that is shifting control of AI infrastructure and supply chains.

variables.name: China–EU trade and industrial competition
variables.description: China and European governments are clashing over market access, industrial policy and strategic sectors—especially autos and green technologies—as Europe deploys caps, tariffs and rules to curb Chinese market penetration.
